gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at November 2026 memory prices, a barebones Intel mini PC plus 32 GB of DDR5 costs more than $800 before any SSD (MS-01 $469 + $569.98 kit = $1,038.98), so the only way to get 32 GB under $800 is a box sold with the RAM fitted. For example, TerraMaster's F4-424 Pro costs $759.99 with 32 GB DDR5 included, while TerraMaster sells a single 32 GB stick alone for $699.99.
standout_why: Rival pages checked: bitdoze.com/best-mini-pc-proxmox (cited) lists a Crucial 32 GB DDR5 kit at $569.98 and works out 'barebone + 32GB about $1,239' only for the i9 MS-01. It never connects that to an under-$800 i5 build or to RAM-included boxes. littlecompute.com/best-mini-pc-for-plex (cited) gives no RAM prices and no configured totals. homelabcompass.com (cited) prices the MS-01 at 'about $600 barebones and up' and gives no configured total or 2026 RAM cost. ChatGPT's own answer budgeted '$100 for 32GB DDR5' and '$120–$180 for 32–64GB', which today's prices contradict by about 5x.
decides: Drop the pick ChatGPT kept repeating, a barebones MS-01 or MS-01 SE with RAM added, from 'under $800'. RAM-included units should lead. On the NAS side that is the TerraMaster F4-424 Pro ($759.99, 32 GB, i3-N305 Quick Sync) or the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus ($619.99, 8 GB, which is enough for Docker and Plex but tight for two VMs). On the mini-PC side, only a model sold with RAM at checkout fits. The page should say plainly: price the RAM before you buy a barebones unit.
